headline: Rough estimate, steady wind, daytime. Rate methods are not field-validated; demo numbers are never used as accuracy.
source: docs/METEC_BLS_EVALUATION.md (METEC 2024 controlled releases; offline developer evaluation, 2026-10-28)

methods.label: Gaussian plume, fit per candidate
methods.how: For each assumed source location, a steady Gaussian plume predicts what every methane sensor should read per kg/h in the measured wind. A non-negative least-squares fit gives the rate and how well that location explains the readings; poor fits get no rate.
needs: Methane sensors downwind of the source

methods.label: Gaussian, all sources fitted together
methods.status_label: Evaluated offline on real METEC data
methods.how: Splits the measured enhancement across all candidate sources at once, minute by minute, with steady-wind gates (wind at least 1 m/s, direction spread at most 30 degrees, daytime).
needs: Several sensors seeing the sources from different directions

methods.label: Backward Lagrangian stochastic (bLs)
methods.how: Releases tens of thousands of virtual particles backward in time from each sensor (WindTrax-style) to find where air came from; the residence time over each source gives the response per kg/h.
needs: Turbulence statistics from a sonic anemometer

methods.label: MDLQ (published, Bayesian)
methods.status_label: External reference (Daniels et al. 2026, MIT licence)
methods.how: Estimates leak probability and a rate range for every source from a continuous sensor network, using a Bayesian model.
needs: A multi-sensor network around the site

tests.label: Development set, single releases
tests.note: Not locked in advance; shown for context only

tests.label: Unseen days, single leak (our mast)
tests.note: Failed: both methods read 2-3x high; neighbouring releases and wandering wind

tests.label: All sources together, 10-sensor network
tests.note: Failed for bLs; the Gaussian comparator did well but needs one more locked test

tests.label: All sources together, our single mast
tests.note: Failed for every method: one sensor location cannot separate sources

metric: Share of estimates within a factor of 2 of the recorded release rate (FAC2)
lessons: Refuse unsteady wind: direction spread over 30 degrees, gusty meandering, night.
Fit all candidate sources together; single-source rates break when neighbours release.
Separating sources needs sensors that see them from different directions; one mast is not enough.
Stability must be measured (heat flux), not guessed.
